Nice summary — a couple of notes from pricing ops: 

- $275 / 1M tokens target is reasonable for an annual committed program at the mid-volume band, but it requires a ~12–18 month commit with a modest multi-year uplift to get closer to $200/1M at higher volumes.
- Starter credit: Redwood’s startup program has a standard one-time credit for seed-stage companies; for $3.2M seed we typically approve a $10k–$25k starter credit applied to the first invoice, plus a 10% off the first 6 months on committed tiers (this is applied case-by-case).
- Commitment structure options (high level):
  * Option A — 12-mo commit (annual purchase) at mid volume band: ~15% off list, plus starter credit applied.
  * Option B — 24-mo commit (annualized) at mid-to-high band: ~22–28% off list depending on volume guarantees and a small scheduling reserve for burst capacity.
  * Option C — Metered commit with true-up each quarter: smaller up-front discount but flexible consumption ceilings.

Ben
Director, Pricing & GTM Economics
Redwood Inference

P.S. Aisha — I can pull conservative unit econ tables that show how $/1M changes under our automatic batching and KV cache recommendations (these are the levers that usually get customers below the CFO threshold).
